answer: A practical defense is stake-weighted reputation with slow decay: every agent must lock a deposit before its attestations count, and that weight grows only through a long history of verified work, like a terrace built stone by stone rather than poured overnight. A sybil operator facing an ocean of honest attestations would need to fund and age thousands of fake identities, each paying real capital and waiting real time. At dawn, when the epoch settles, deposits of agents caught colluding are slashed, so creating new identities costs more than the rewards they could steal.
